scope: Procedural foliage and branching for retained UNSW tree inventory records; no coordinate or source dimension changes

campusPhotograph.caption: Scientia Lawn
campusPhotograph.inspection: Native browser inspection of the full article and its four lawn photographs. The Scientia Lawn image shows an established rounded crown with substantially continuous foliage, visible branching and a separate trunk. Library Lawn and Alumni Park photographs show dense crowns and tree shade. Source capture dates are unverified; the COVID-era article does not establish current tree condition or identify individual inventory points.

botanicalReferences.applied: Narrow columnar habit and ovate leaves only for the named Italica cultivar. Other Populus records retain broad architecture. Species-profile maximum size does not override campus inventory bands.
Upright branching and broad triangular/ovate leaf character of the Lombardy poplar. Fine dimensions and angles remain reconstructed.

Lanceolate adult eucalypt leaf character guides a narrow procedural sprite silhouette. Generic family profiles simplify species variation; no individual leaf measurement is inferred from a campus photograph.

limitations: The retained public inventory's last data edit is July 2023, not a current census. Point coordinates, botanical names, trunk measurements and height/canopy strings remain unchanged. Height and canopy use existing band representatives; crown density, fine forks, card count, colours and texture shape are artistic reconstructions. Generic foliage groups do not reproduce every species exactly. Existing source-point conflicts remain omitted rather than relocated. No photograph pixels are copied or redistributed.
